te: The Nong Han Kumphawapi wetland, and floods and pollution in Prachin Buri
se: The meeting noted an overview of managing, conserving and restoring Thailand's wetlands, the role of the Department of Water Resources, legal limits and cooperation between agencies, using the Nong Han Kumphawapi wetland in Udon Thani as a case, and considered a feasibility study for surveying the Red Lotus Sea wetland to protect biodiversity. It then considered floods in Prachin Buri and water pollution from an industrial waste plant located in a national reserved forest.
it: The Nong Han Kumphawapi wetland, Udon Thani
Floods and water pollution from an industrial waste plant, Prachin Buri

Report on adding value to seized timber in a systematic way
se: The meeting noted the study report on promoting and adding value to seized timber in a systematic way, which proposes how the state should store, sell or use seized timber to create economic value, and reduce the amount of seized timber by preventing illegal logging. The report says seized timber is held mainly by four agencies: the Royal Forest Department, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, the Department of Marine and Coastal Resources and the Customs Department, and sums up problems found on visits to timber storage sites.
it: Report on promoting and adding value to seized timber

te: Meeting summary video · Report on adding value to seized timber in a systematic way
Draft report on PM2.5 dust, and revising laws on teak and economic timber
se: The committee considered the draft report of the study on PM2.5 dust in Bangkok, its surrounding provinces and the upper North, covering the situation, problems and policy proposals. The meeting added comments such as strict law enforcement and support for biotechnology to break down farm waste instead of burning it. It also considered revising laws on teak and economic timber in the North.
it: Draft report of the study on PM2.5 dust
Revising laws on teak and economic timber in the North

te: Meeting summary video · Draft report on PM2.5 dust, and revising laws on teak and economic timber
Subcommittees and advisers for fiscal year 2027, and a complaint about rock digging in Phang Nga
se: The meeting resolved to set up three subcommittees for fiscal year 2027: Land Resources (chaired by Mr. Jirasak Chukwamdee), Whole-System Water Management, Pollution and Environment (chaired by Miss Ratchaneekorn Thongthip) and Climate Change and Air Pollution (chaired by Mr. Chavaphon Wattanavekin), and appointed honorary advisers. It then took up a complaint about illegal rock digging that led to a landslide in Bang Toei subdistrict, Mueang Phang Nga district, and noted the observations and recommendations. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Three subcommittees set up for fiscal year 2027
Honorary advisers appointed for fiscal year 2027
Complaint about rock digging that led to a landslide, Phang Nga

Meeting 36/2569 · Committee on Natural Resources and Environment
Restoring forests, stopping encroachment and adding green space in towns and the countryside
se: The committee studied forest management, restoring forest areas, stopping encroachment and adding green space in towns and rural areas, looking at the permanent reforestation project in honour of His Majesty King Bhumibol Adulyadej The Great on the 50th anniversary of his accession to the throne in 1994, carried out from 1994 to 2007, and hearing views from experts and the private tree sector.
it: Restoring forests and adding green space in towns and the countryside

te: Complaint about encroachment on headwater forest to grow ginger, Chai Prakan district, Chiang Mai
se: The committee considered a complaint about encroachment on headwater forest to grow ginger in Chai Prakan district, Chiang Mai, with the Royal Forest Department, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, the Forest Industry Organization, the National Land Policy Office and the Chiang Mai natural resources and environment office invited to explain land use in the area, inspections, legal action and the limits of prevention. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Complaint about encroachment on headwater forest to grow ginger, Chai Prakan district, Chiang Mai

te: Forest encroachment in Chom Bueng district, Ratchaburi
se: The meeting noted its findings on forest encroachment in Rang Bua and Dan Thap Tako subdistricts, Chom Bueng district, Ratchaburi, with the Royal Forest Department, the Department of Lands and the Natural Resources and Environmental Crime Suppression Division invited. The Royal Forest Department said villagers asked to set up a community forest in 2019, and checks found part of the area in a national reserved forest, while nearby land has title documents and land reform land, and there is a complaint that documents may have been issued wrongly, so the agencies concerned were asked to check.
it: Forest encroachment in Chom Bueng district, Ratchaburi

te: Complaint opposing the Khlong Wang Tanot reservoir project, Chanthaburi
se: The meeting noted initial information on a complaint opposing the Khlong Wang Tanot reservoir project in Chanthaburi, whose budget the Cabinet approved on 5 August 2026 to supply irrigation, ease floods and serve industry. The complainants are concerned about the loss of forest in Khao Sip Ha Chan National Park, a source of food and home for wildlife and wild elephants, the accuracy of the environmental and health impact assessment (EHIA), and the distribution of water from existing reservoirs. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Complaint opposing the Khlong Wang Tanot reservoir project, Chanthaburi

te: Caring for and restoring headwater forests in the North
se: The committee studied the management and restoration of headwater forests in the North, with the Office of the Permanent Secretary for Natural Resources and Environment, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation and the Royal Forest Department invited to explain the current situation, conservation and restoration, and problems. The national parks department said the North has about 107 million rai of forest, most class 1 and 2 headwater forest in protected areas is still intact, and villagers living in protected areas are being helped with farmland rights.
it: Managing and restoring headwater forests in the North

te: The Mae La Ka Rong local wetland in Sing Buri
se: The committee studied how to keep developing the local wetland along the Mae La Ka Rong stream in Sing Buri, with the agencies concerned and experts invited. The Department of Water Resources said it took over wetland work in 2022 and is the lead coordinating agency, including checking whether development projects lie in wetlands.
it: Developing the Mae La Ka Rong local wetland, Sing Buri

te: Following up land reform documents in Bang Lamung, and construction effects on Ko Pha Ngan
se: The committee followed up the complaint about land reform documents in Bang Lamung district, Chon Buri. The Chon Buri land reform office said a stream had been surveyed into plots in the past, and the plots have been redrawn to leave out the stream and return the area to the Royal Forest Department, which confirmed the area is part of a national reserved forest. The committee then took up a complaint asking for a check of environmental effects from building hotel and resort-type buildings at Haad Salad, Ko Pha Ngan district, Surat Thani, where cement water from construction was found flowing into the sea and coral reefs. Complaints are claims that the agencies are still checking.
it: Follow-up on land reform documents, Bang Lamung district, Chon Buri
Construction effects on the sea and coral reefs, Ko Pha Ngan
